reviewer: Claude (simulated category judge, not an official judge), Round Four, 11 October 2026

reasons.A1: No quality measurement. The paper itself says 'A matched quality comparison is still needed'. A08 tests utilities, not quality.
reasons.A2: The A10 QLoRA script (L01) is code, not a completed adaptation. No adapter, trainer state or serving record. A09 overlap blocks uplift claims. Copilot use is ordinary.
reasons.A3: Two reported quarters. A/B and prompt-version code (L02–L04, L10) exists with no populated results. Mechanism is not sustained value.
reasons.A4: 257 person-days, review-deducted, with a nested 8→4 hour task. This is attributed and coherent, but there is no ledger, approval export or retained-quality check (S01).
reasons.A5: Reported use by the client assurance team only. No satisfaction or outcome data. The 85% figure is undefined.

editorial_fixes.passage: Microsoft Copilot 365 supported the first delivery phase.
editorial_fixes.replace: Microsoft 365 Copilot supported the first delivery phase.

editorial_fixes.passage: The accessibility team reports 85 per cent automation within its workflow.
editorial_fixes.replace: Delete the paragraph unless the numerator, denominator and period are supplied. If they are: 'Across [period], [n] of [N] defined accessibility checks ran without manual initiation.'

Reduce to one paragraph: 'Separately, the team has built local prototypes with governance code (prompt versioning, A/B assignment, fail-closed release gates). These are not deployed to the client and are not included in reported benefits.' Use the recovered space for the delivery method and the quality-review procedure.

editorial_fixes.passage: the number of projects evaluated is not stated in the source
editorial_fixes.replace: Drop it from the main sentence. State the estate size only once evaluated counts are available.
Use one spelling (IntelliPerf, or the product's registered form) consistently across both papers.

absent: Quarterly task ledger and review deductions

reasons.N1: The only primary visual (N01) shows a FAILED alert with count 4 and 104.6% volume. No passing acceptance record.
reasons.N2: The KQL workload derivation, 1x–4x profiles and cache reproduction are well described, but all come from digests. Environment comparability is unevidenced.
reasons.N3: Three releases are reported with no dates, acceptance records or observation window. The 90% figures lack timings.
reasons.N4: Goals and resources are clear. Results are narrative (N04), and the 50× capacity baseline is unresolved.
reasons.N5: The strongest criterion. The 57/64 telemetry gap, false-success exits and cache investigation are well evaluated, though still digest-sourced.

editorial_fixes.passage: Performance validation approach and observed results
editorial_fixes.replace: Performance validation approach and reported results

editorial_fixes.passage: It scales test environments to production-like capacity before execution
editorial_fixes.replace: It scales test environments to a configured target capacity before execution; comparability with production is assessed per service.

editorial_fixes.passage: AI supported the engineering of these capabilities… (whole paragraph)
editorial_fixes.replace: Delete it. It is irrelevant to N1–N5, overlaps the AI paper's account-wide claim, and frees characters.

reasons.I1: A coherent ownership model, but the paper concedes it is 'an application of existing test and pipeline technology'.
reasons.I2: The driver is clear. The implementation is described from S02 only, with no repository or pipeline history.
reasons.I3: No evidence of a boundary pushed. Wider adoption is 'not yet established'.
reasons.I4: Five teams are reported. No results are claimed or measured.
reasons.I5: The maintenance obligation and triage route are reasoned, but there is no worked triage example.

editorial_fixes.passage: Its operational benefits remain to be verified through contribution and run records.
editorial_fixes.replace: Variants of this caveat appear about five times. State it once in section 4 and use the space for a concrete worked flow (tag → selection → failure → triage → owner fix).
Add the pipeline stage design, the triage decision rules and a comparison with the prior central-pack practice. All must be supported by records.

council_recommendation.verdict: 4/5 on every criterion is not defensible for any paper. A10 adds implementation evidence, not outcomes, so AI scores are unchanged on A1, A4 and A5. Polish and repeated review are not evidence.
cross_paper_conflicts: The AI paper's account-wide 257 days could absorb NFT Copilot/PowerShell work and shared-regression effort. State explicitly in each paper that no saving is counted twice.
The AI paper's local IntelliSec/IntelliA11y/Inteliperf material weakens the single client-project scope. The organiser may treat it as a separate, non-deployed entry.
All three papers name the same client. The identity must be supplied to the organiser under the rules, recorded separately and never disclosed.
council_recommendation.limits_and_privacy: Summaries are estimated at about 88, 86 and 98 words. The Innovation summary is near the limit, so recount with hyphen rules. NFT main text is estimated close to 14,600 characters; verify with a counter before submission. No confidential identifiers found. Internal tool names (Pulse, Delivery Excellence) are acceptable but optional.
council_recommendation.priority: 1) S01 ledger and approval export. 2) N-series raw run and acceptance records. 3) S02 contribution history. 4) An independent AI quality comparison. Do not invent any of these.
